entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9908"/><div sID="gen17597" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9908"/><hi type="bold">6. wild asses--</hi>They repair to "the high places" most exposed to the winds, which they "snuff in" to relieve their thirst.<div eID="gen17597" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17598" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dragons--</hi>jackals [Henderson].<div eID="gen17598" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17599" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eyes--</hi>which are usually most keen in detecting grass or water from the "heights," so much so that the traveller guesses from their presence that there must be herbage and water near; but now "their eyes fail." Rather the reference is to the great boas and python serpents which raise a large portion of their body up in a vertical column ten or twelve feet high, to survey the neighborhood above the surrounding bushes, while with open jaws they drink in the air. These giant serpents originated the widely spread notions which typified the deluge and all destructive agents under the form of a dragon or monster serpent; hence, the dragon temples always near water, in Asia, Africa, and Britain; for example, at Abury, in Wiltshire; a symbol of the ark is often associated with the dragon as the preserver from the waters [Kitto, Biblical Cyclopædia]. <div eID="gen17599" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9920"/><div sID="gen17623" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9920"/><hi type="bold">18. go about--</hi>that is, shall have to migrate into a land of exile. Horsley translates, "go trafficking about the land (see <reference osisRef="Jer.5.31">Jr 5:31</reference>, Margin; <reference osisRef="2Cor.4.2">2Co 4:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.2.3">2Pe 2:3</reference>), and take no knowledge" (that is, pay no regard to the miseries before their eyes) (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.3">Is 1:3</reference>; 58:3). <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9923"/><div sID="gen17628" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9923"/><hi type="bold">21. us--</hi>"the throne of Thy glory" may be the object of "abhor not" ("reject not"); or "Zion" (<reference osisRef="Jer.14.19">Jr 14:19</reference>).<div eID="gen17628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17629" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">throne of thy glory--</hi>Jerusalem, or, the temple, called God's "footstool" and "habitation" (<reference osisRef="1Chr.28.2">1Ch 28:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.132.5">Psa 132:5</reference>).<div eID="gen17629" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17630" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy covenant--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.106.45">Psa 106:45</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.9.19">Da 9:19</reference>). <div eID="gen17630" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 21. us-- "the throne of Thy glory" may be the object of "abhor not" ("reject not"); or "Zion" ( Jr 14:19 ). throne of thy glory-- Jerusalem, or, the temple, called God's "footstool" and "habitation" ( 1Ch 28:2 ; Psa 132:5 ). thy covenant-- ( Psa 106:45 ; Da 9:19 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9924"/><div sID="gen17631" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9924"/><hi type="bold">22. vanities--</hi>idols (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.21">De 32:21</reference>).<div eID="gen17631" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17632" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rain--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Zech.10.1">Zec 10:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.10.2">2</reference>).<div eID="gen17632" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17633" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heavens--</hi>namely, of themselves without God (<reference osisRef="Matt.5.45">Mt 5:45</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.14.17">Ac 14:17</reference>); they are not the First Cause, and ought not to be deified, as they were by the heathen. The disjunctive "or" favors Calvin's explanation: "Not even the heavens themselves can give rain, much less can the idol vanities."<div eID="gen17633" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17634" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">art not thou he--</hi>namely, who canst give rain? <chapter eID="Jer.14"/>
entries.content_plain: 22. vanities-- idols ( De 32:21 ). rain-- ( Zec 10:1 , 2 ). heavens-- namely, of themselves without God ( Mt 5:45 ; Ac 14:17 ); they are not the First Cause, and ought not to be deified, as they were by the heathen. The disjunctive "or" favors Calvin's explanation: "Not even the heavens themselves can give rain, much less can the idol vanities." art not thou he-- namely, who canst give rain?
